outcome_analysis.explanation: The official completed evaluations make this a serial_only_pass pair: parallel passed 38/40 and serial passed 40/40. The direct process difference is not simply that parallel used agents; it is that after building a mostly working package, the parallel parent launched a six-way audit workflow, one child observed a formatting IndexError, and the parent then blocked on TaskOutput until the workflow was killed. Serial performed the analogous verification loop locally, applied the empty-value formatting guard, reran checks, cleaned the tree, and completed normally. The exact official failed-test names are unavailable, so the coordination episode is a supported contributor to the discordance, not a proven sole cause.
parallel_contributors: Six broad verifier children ran late and consumed the remaining closure budget.
A child-observed formatPair IndexError was not returned to or integrated by the parent.
The parent blocked waiting for aggregate TaskOutput and final.txt remained empty.
serial_contributors: The parent directly fixed the empty-value formatPair guard and reran checks.
The serial run completed local tests, API checks, tox packaging, cleanup, and final response without delegation.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel likely retained at least one ordinary implementation defect around empty-value formatting, while serial added a direct bool(value) guard.
evaluator_effects: Official result details list counts only, not hidden test names; no evaluator anomaly is visible.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: supported comparative contributors, not an exclusive root cause
